Toolset overview

Source: vignettes/tools.qmd

This vignette explains why each rairai tool exists and which AI-agent workflows it supports. Use it together with the numbered design principles in vignettes/design.qmd when deciding whether a tool is useful, redundant, or better expressed as part of a higher-level workflow.

Target workflows

The toolset should be judged against common workflows where an AI agent benefits from R-specific structure and evidence.

W1 — Understand a symbol

Answer: what is this object, where is it defined, and where is it used? Useful tools should resolve a name to candidates, return a definition location, list references, and make ambiguity explicit.

W2 — Prepare a safe code change

Before editing, an agent should find the relevant object, inspect the source range with its normal file-reading tools, understand affected call sites, and find related tests and exported API status.

W3 — Refactor without guessing

For renaming, moving, or restructuring code, an agent needs a map of definitions, references, exported names, namespace declarations, and tests. rairai should prefer previewable evidence over tools that silently mutate code.

W4 — Diagnose a failure or warning

When tests or checks fail, an agent needs to connect messages to source locations and package context. Tools should help inspect the relevant object, references, dependencies, documentation, and namespace state.

W5 — Explore an unfamiliar package

An agent joining a codebase needs quick orientation: package files, dependencies, namespace exports/imports, file-scoped symbols, and important symbols. This should not require reading every source file in full.

W6 — Add or update tests

When changing behavior, an agent needs to find the implementation, related tests, and call sites. Tools should identify objects and affected files, while ordinary file and shell tools handle reading, editing, and running tests.

Tool surface and package roots

serve() is the only exported R function. It exposes 21 public MCP tools that accept names, paths, scopes, and package concepts. Calls in this guide use MCP argument notation, not exported R functions.

The 19 package-local tools use the immutable canonical default selected by serve(path = ...). To inspect another directory, repeat its native absolute package_root on every applicable call. Omitted, NULL, or empty selectors use the default; relative paths, tilde paths, and file URIs are not root selectors. The directory must exist and is canonicalized, including symlink resolution. Resolved responses report the effective root in package_root. The CRAN tools cran_search and cran_package have no root selector.

path and context_path filter within the effective root; they do not select a package. package retains each tool’s installed-documentation, external-function, or imported-package meaning. In particular, package_docs() defaults to local documentation, while help_search() without package searches local and installed help. External function signatures remain unsupported by function_formals(); use the help tools instead.

Roots are unrestricted process-readable directories. File listings and package-role readers can disclose more than conventional package metadata, and responses disclose canonical absolute host paths. Within-package containment is not a race-free sandbox; process or container permissions provide strong filesystem confinement.

Usability goals

Design tool names, descriptions, and outputs so that an agent is nudged toward a small number of obvious first moves:

  • use package_overview() when entering an unfamiliar package;
  • use symbols() when looking for code entities by name, kind, or file scope;
  • use definition() and references() when preparing a targeted edit;
  • use refactor_context() when the requested change may affect many call sites or exported names;
  • use tests_for() when changing behavior;
  • use package_docs(), help_search(), and help_page() for documentation and external/package-qualified function questions.

Avoid exposing multiple tools that appear to answer the same question unless the difference changes the agent’s next action. If a distinction mainly reflects an implementation backend, keep it private.

Where useful, responses should include compact routing hints such as counts, ambiguity status, returned path/range fields, and suggested lower-level tools to call next. These hints should be structured fields rather than prose summaries so agents can act on them reliably.

Tool purposes

This section describes the toolset from the perspective of an AI coding agent. Tools are grouped by the task they help an agent perform, not by the underlying data source used to implement them.

Package orientation tools

Use these tools when the agent needs to understand the package shape before choosing files or symbols to inspect. They provide R-package context that ordinary file readers and text search do not reconstruct reliably.

  • package_overview: default first look at DESCRIPTION, NAMESPACE, package file layout, tests, vignettes, source symbols, and R6 classes.
  • package_dependencies: read dependency declarations from DESCRIPTION, including direct and optionally indirect dependencies.
  • package_files: list package files by package-oriented scope, with optional metadata such as line counts, size, or modification time.
  • package_namespace: read exports, imported objects by package, S3 method registrations, and dynamic library declarations from NAMESPACE.
  • package_docs: browse local or installed package documentation, including help topics, vignette and NEWS summaries, and next-tool hints.
  • package_news: read NEWS.md or NEWS content for the local package or an installed package.
  • package_vignettes: list available vignettes or retrieve a specific vignette as plain text.
  • cran_search: search ranked CRAN package metadata for candidate packages.
  • cran_package: look up DESCRIPTION-like CRAN metadata for one exact package name.

Preferred workflow routes

  • Unfamiliar package: call package_overview(), then symbols(), package_files(), or package_docs() for the relevant area.
  • Documentation map: call package_docs() to browse help topics, vignette availability, and NEWS availability without a search query.
  • Specific function or object: call symbols(query = ..., exact = TRUE) or definition(name = ...), then read the returned source range with the agent’s normal file-reading tool.
  • Behavior change: call definition(), references(), and tests_for() before editing.
  • Rename or structural refactor: call refactor_context() first, then inspect the resolved declaration, references, namespace/export information, and tests.
  • Test failure: use the file/range from the failure when available, then call symbols(path = ...), definition(), references(), or package_namespace() depending on whether the problem is local code, call-site impact, or package API state.
  • Documentation lookup: call help_search(query = ..., package = ...) when the topic is unknown, then help_page(topic = ..., sections = ...) for selected sections.
  • R6 code: call r6_classes() or r6_class() before falling back to generic symbol search, because R6 member structure is easier to inspect with R6-aware tools.

Symbol and source navigation tools

Use symbols() to find code entities or decide what source range to read next. Package source indexing covers flat R/*.[Rr] files.

  • symbols
    • Purpose: find or list Tree-sitter-indexed package-local source symbols using optional query, file path, kind, and exact-match filters. With path supplied, it lists or searches symbols in that file. Without path, it searches package source symbols. Ambiguous matches are returned as structured candidates rather than silently resolved.
    • Example uses:
      • symbols(path = "R/foo.R") lists symbols in one file.
      • symbols(query = "parse", exact = FALSE) searches matching names across the package.
      • symbols(query = "parse", path = "R/foo.R", exact = FALSE) searches matching names within one file.
    • Workflows: W1, W2, W5, W6.

Definition, reference, and impact tools

  • definition
    • Purpose: resolve a symbol name to one canonical definition. If the name is ambiguous, return candidates with enough information for the agent to narrow the request instead of choosing one silently.
    • Workflows: W1, W2, W6.
  • references
    • Purpose: resolve a symbol name and return role-classified syntactic impact reference locations. The resolved declaration is reported separately from usage references; path filters candidate resolution, while the reference search scope is package-wide and includes tests by default.
    • Workflows: W1, W2, W3, W6.
  • refactor_context
    • Purpose: return a complete refactor-readiness context for a symbol by name: resolved declaration, references, namespace/export status, and related tests when available. Return candidates when the symbol is ambiguous.
    • Workflows: W3.

Function inspection tools

Use this tool when the agent needs to call or modify a function without loading the target package.

  • function_formals
    • Purpose: return a local package function’s call signature, parameters, and defaults from the Tree-sitter source index. External or package-qualified requests return an explicit unsupported result with help_page() and help_search() next-tool hints. The tool does not load or execute the target package to recover signatures.
    • Workflows: W1, W2, W6.

Test and documentation discovery tools

  • tests_for: search test files for mentions of a symbol name and return compact 1-based location strings. Works entirely from source with no package loading required.
  • package_docs: browse the documentation map for the local source package or an installed package without requiring a query.
  • help_search: search help topics by function name, alias, title, or concept.
  • help_page: retrieve one R help page as plain text, with optional section filtering and character limits.
  • package_vignettes: list available package vignettes or retrieve one vignette.
  • package_news: inspect recent or version-specific behavior changes when diagnosing failures or preparing user-visible changes.

R6 structure tools

  • r6_classes: list all R6 classes defined in the package’s flat R/*.[Rr] source files with exact source locations and inheritance relationships.
  • r6_class: return the full structure of a named R6 class, including public, private, and active members.
  • r6_method: return the compact source location and exact source text for a specific R6 class method.
  • r6_method_references: find call sites that use $method() syntax for a named R6 method, with target-resolution metadata for the requested class and method.

Questions for tool review

When reviewing the toolset, ask:

  1. Which workflows does this tool support?
  2. Which design principles justify its shape?
  3. Is it a preferred LLM-facing tool, a lower-level primitive, or redundant?
  4. Would a combined workflow tool reduce repeated calls without hiding ambiguity?
  5. Does the tool provide R-package or R-language intelligence that ordinary file/search/shell tools do not already provide?
  6. Are optional arguments robust if an MCP client fills in NULL, an empty string, a schema default, or the first enum value instead of omitting them?
